title: The big storm, his grandfather, and his great-aunt who read French
summary: He recalls his grandfather's account of storm damage in New Orleans, relatives living in the city, and his French-reading seamstress great-aunt.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Now, I was going to ask you about dates now. Where were you when the big storm was? Were you in the city? Are we out of there?

No, that big storm, I remember my grandfather was living. And I don't know whether he was here, but he had came to New Orleans after the storm. And he had... You know, my grandfather never did like New Orleans. I don't know why. And he had went down to the... I remember he was describing to the other sisters and brothers about how the French market was all... The top and thing was all tore down and everything. And my Aunt Bella was living here then, I'm sure, yeah. And he had another son. This is my Uncle Roscoe, yeah. And another son from my Uncle Thetto. I remember we're living here in New Orleans. And my Aunt Bridget was living here. My Aunt Maggie was living in here. And my great auntie, that would be my mother's sister, Big Nenang. She was a very dark woman with very cold, black hands. She could read and write French. Because I never did learn it. But I mean, from a kid I never did like French or Creole. But I mean, my sister, she had a chance to... I mean, not Creole, French. And it was told to me that she either went to France or she was instructed by some white people that taught her. Because she was, it seems, by trade. She was what you call a old-made woman that never got married. And she made her living by sewing. She was a very good sewer. And she could... She spoke very bad English. But anything in real... And she didn't understand Creole so much. I mean, but if you spoke real French, she could really understand. She could write French. She could write it, yeah. Yeah. Now let's say we were...
Just getting back to the city. Yeah.
Now I say we moved here. We left down to, I say, about 1915. I remember.
